clips.title: The story
paras: Tatternack Steelforge seeks new ore in Thousand Needles to strengthen the Horde’s arms. The blacksmith in Camp Taurajo sends you south to bring back a sample for testing.

Tatternack Steelforge works as a blacksmith in Camp Taurajo, under Orgrimmar’s direct scrutiny. He has already supplied weapons made from local centaur armaments, but still wants to prove his craft to Warchief Thrall. Travelers passing through showed him a strange piece of ore taken from a kobold to the south. When they refused to sell it, Tatternack took their refusal as an insult to his craft and the Horde.

You leave the flat plains of the southern Barrens for the towering canyon mazes of Thousand Needles. Kobold diggers tunnel through its crags and cliffs. Bring back unrefined chunks taken directly from them, and Tatternack can judge whether the raw mineral can be forged into weapons worthy of Thrall’s war effort.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Adventurer, you have done well in helping me in the past. The warchief is pleased thus far with what I've accomplished, and asks me to continue with renewed determination. My honor dictates that I give you proper recognition to the warchief for all you have done, but first I would ask you for your help again.

Travelers recently came from the south from a place called Thousand Needles. There they killed a kobold who had an unusual ore sample, but they would not sell it. I want a sample of that ore to examine.

clips.title: Progress
paras: I saw the travelers again—the ones that would not sell me a sample of the ore. I spit at them for not helping the warchief.
May they die in battle like cowards and not like warriors as should be the right of all people who ally themselves with the Horde.

clips.title: Completion
paras: A good sample, friend. A good sample indeed.
Those travelers can no longer lord over me the ore they found, now that you have been successful.
I shall get to work on it immediately. If it proves strong enough, I will send a weapon crafted from the material back to the warchief to show him our success.
I shall not forget your help, adventurer.
